title: CommandOutput
description: Every document the CLI prints with --json. Scan results (list, show), check results, config results and tools results carry schema_version 1, which changes only on breaking changes.

CaptureFailure.description: What `debug capture --json` prints when nothing was recorded.

tool.description: The tool id that was asked for.

CaptureFailure.title: CaptureFailure

CaptureOutcome.description: What `debug capture --json` prints after writing a capture file.

tool.description: The tool id that was captured.

destination.description: Path of the capture file that was written.

exit_code.description:
Exit code of the captured command, the tool's version command or a provider's listing
command (recorded even when non-zero).

CaptureOutcome.title: CaptureOutcome

CatalogProvider.description:
A provider: code that reports a version manager's installs, including ones not on
PATH.

id.description: Provider id, which is also the `source` of the installs it reports (e.g. `nvm`).

os.description: The operating systems it runs on.

tools.description: Ids of the tools it reports installs for.

CatalogProvider.title: CatalogProvider

CatalogTool.description: A tool VersionBar knows how to detect.

id.description: Stable tool id, as used on the command line and in scan results.

os.description: The operating systems it is detected on; elsewhere scans leave it out.

custom.description:
True when its definition comes from the user config file (a custom tool, possibly
replacing a built-in of the same id).

CatalogTool.title: CatalogTool

CheckResult.description:
The result of `check --json`: one live scan, then every requirement tested against the
active install of its tool. The exit code is 0 exactly when `passed` is true.

schema_version.description: Changes only on breaking changes to this format; the same counter as ScanResult's.

scanned_at.description: When the scan ran, RFC 3339 in UTC.

requirements.description: One entry per requirement, in the order given.

CheckResult.title: CheckResult

ConfigProblem.description: One thing wrong with the user config file.

message.description: Human-readable description of the problem; not for parsing.

ConfigProblem.title: ConfigProblem

ConfigResult.description:
The result of `config --json`, the preferences query: where the user config file is
and the preferences it sets. Read live; nothing is run.

Exit code 0 when the config is usable (absent counts: defaults apply), 3 when it is not,
in which case `problems` says why and `preferences` is null.

schema_version.description: Changes only on breaking changes to this format; the same counter as ScanResult's.

config_path.description: Absolute path of the user config file, whether or not it exists.

config_exists.description: Whether there is a file at `config_path`. False means every default applies.

problems.description: Everything wrong with the file; empty when it is usable.

preferences.description: The preferences in effect, or null when the file is unusable (see `problems`).

ConfigResult.title: ConfigResult

FailureOutcome.description: Why nothing was captured. More values may be added without a breaking change; handle unknown ones.

version.description: The version as the tool prints it, vendor suffixes included.

path.description: Absolute path of the executable that was run.

source.description: `path`, or the id of the provider that reported the install.

via.description: The manager whose shim serves this install, or null.

raw.description: Decoded version output the version was parsed from, or null.

Preferences.description: The preferences the app needs from the config file, defaults filled in.

update_check.description:
Whether the app may check for VersionBar updates. When false it must make no update
requests.

pinned.description:
Tool ids to show first, in this order. Each id appears at most once in `pinned` and
`order` together; ids of tools that are not in a scan are allowed and are skipped.

order.description: Tool ids to show after the pinned ones, in this order.

Preferences.title: Preferences

RequirementOutcome.description: `passed`: met. Every other value is a failure: `unmet` (the active version is outside the range), `not-comparable` (the active version has no leading number to compare), `missing`, `error` or `timeout` (the tool has no usable active install; same meaning as the tool status). More values may be added without a schema_version bump; handle unknown ones.

RequirementResult.description: The verdict on one requirement given to `check`.

requirement.description: The requirement exactly as given, e.g. `node@>=20`.

tool.description: Tool id the requirement is about.

spec.description: The version spec after `@` (e.g. `>=20,<23`), or null for a presence-only requirement.

version.description: Version of the active install as the tool prints it, or null when there is none.

path.description: Absolute path of the active install, or null when there is none.

message.description: Human-readable explanation of the verdict; not for parsing.

RequirementResult.title: RequirementResult

ScanResult.description:
The result of one live scan: what `list --json` and `show --json` print.

`platform` and `status` may gain values without a schema_version bump; handle
unknown ones (for example with a default branch).

schema_version.description: Changes only on breaking changes to this format.

scanned_at.description: When the scan ran, RFC 3339 in UTC.

tools.description:
`list`: every tool known on this OS, missing ones included, except those the user config
hides; its pinned and ordered tools come first. `show`: the requested ones, in request order.

ScanResult.title: ScanResult

Tool.description: One tool and every install of it that was found.

id.description: Stable tool id, as used on the command line (e.g. `git`).

active.description: The install that runs when you type the command, or null when there is none.

installs.description:
Every install found: the active one first, then the other PATH installs, then those
providers report (which are never active, so a tool with no active install may still have
some).

notes.description: Human-readable explanations for the status (why missing, what failed); not for parsing.

Tool.title: Tool

ToolStatus.description: More values may be added without a schema_version bump; handle unknown ones.

ToolsResult.description:
The result of `tools --json`: every tool and provider this VersionBar knows, on every
operating system. Read live from the built-ins and the user config file; nothing is run.

schema_version.description: Changes only on breaking changes to this format; the same counter as ScanResult's.

platform.description: The operating system this ran on.

tools.description:
Built-in tools by file name, then custom tools in config file order; a custom tool
with a built-in's id takes that built-in's place. Hidden tools are included.

providers.description: Every provider, in the order its installs are reported.

ToolsResult.title: ToolsResult
